description: The LLM Observability Dashboard provides analytics for LLM token usage, cost breakdown, and provider performance. Displays summary metric cards, cost-over-time and cost-by-model charts, phase cost breakdown, provider latency distribution, a 7-day moving average cost trend line, and a per-run cost table. Data sourced via Tauri commands (SQLite) and web API (PostgreSQL) with TanStack Query caching.

groups.name: Summary Cards
groups.description: Four metric cards at the top of the dashboard showing aggregate LLM usage statistics: Total Cost (formatted as dollars from cents, with provider count subtitle), Total Tokens (input + output with K/M suffixes, with in/out breakdown subtitle), Total Calls (with unique model count subtitle), and Avg Cost/Call (with average duration subtitle when available). These cards give the user an instant overview of LLM spend and usage volume for the selected time range.

assertions.description: The user can see a 'Total Cost' metric card displaying the total LLM spend formatted as dollars (e.g., '$12.34') with a subtitle showing the number of unique providers used
assertions.precondition: LLM analytics data has loaded successfully

assertions.description: The user can see a 'Total Tokens' metric card displaying the combined input + output token count with K/M suffixes, and a subtitle showing the input/output breakdown (e.g., '1.2M in / 800.0K out')
assertions.precondition: LLM analytics data has loaded successfully

assertions.description: The user can see a 'Total Calls' metric card displaying the number of LLM API calls made, with a subtitle showing the count of unique models used
assertions.precondition: LLM analytics data has loaded successfully

assertions.description: The user can see an 'Avg Cost/Call' metric card displaying the average cost per LLM call formatted as dollars, with an optional subtitle showing average duration in milliseconds when available
assertions.precondition: LLM analytics data has loaded successfully

groups.name: Time Range Selection
groups.description: A dropdown selector and refresh button in the dashboard header that controls the time window for all analytics data. Options are 'Last 24 hours' (1d), 'Last 7 days' (7d, default), 'Last 30 days' (30d), and 'All time' (all). Changing the selection triggers a re-fetch of all Tauri-backed queries with the corresponding days parameter. The refresh button manually invalidates all cached queries.

assertions.description: The user can see a time range dropdown selector with a clock icon, defaulting to 'Last 7 days', that allows filtering all dashboard data by time period
The time range dropdown contains exactly four options: 'Last 24 hours', 'Last 7 days', 'Last 30 days', and 'All time'
The user can click a 'Refresh analytics' button (with aria-label) to manually re-fetch all dashboard data without changing the time range
Changing the time range selection causes all charts and summary cards to update, reflecting data from the newly selected period via the useLlmAnalytics hook re-fetching with the new days parameter

expectedState.description: Selecting a different time range causes all Tauri queries to re-fetch with the updated days parameter and chart data to reflect the new time window

groups.name: Cost Trends
groups.description: A dedicated cost trend chart that fetches its own data independently from the web backend via useCostTrends (fetch API â†’ PostgreSQL). Shows a Recharts LineChart with two lines: 'Daily Cost' (solid line with dots) and '7-Day Average' (dashed line, computed client-side via 7-day rolling window). Displays summary stats above the chart: Total spend, Avg/day cost, and Trend direction (up/down/flat icon). The trend direction compares the average of the last 7 days against the previous 7 days, with a 5% threshold.

assertions.precondition: Cost trends data has loaded and at least 7 days of data exist

groups.name: Dashboard Loading & Error States
groups.description: The dashboard handles three non-data states: (1) Loading â€” a centered spinning RefreshCw icon while any Tauri query is in-flight; (2) Error â€” an AlertTriangle icon with 'Failed to load LLM analytics', the error message text, and a 'Retry' button that triggers refresh; (3) Empty â€” a CreditCard icon with 'No LLM usage data available' and 'Run some workflows to start collecting LLM analytics' when summary is null or total_calls is 0. Individual chart components also have their own empty states when their specific data arrays are empty.

assertions.description: While LLM analytics data is being fetched, the dashboard shows a centered spinning refresh icon (RefreshCw with animate-spin) instead of any dashboard content
When data fetching fails, the dashboard displays an AlertTriangle icon, the text 'Failed to load LLM analytics', and the specific error message below it
When an error occurs, a 'Retry' button is displayed that calls the refresh function to re-fetch all analytics data
When no LLM usage data exists (summary is null or total_calls is 0), the dashboard shows a CreditCard icon, 'No LLM usage data available', and 'Run some workflows to start collecting LLM analytics'
The empty state includes guidance text 'Run some workflows to start collecting LLM analytics' to help the user understand what action is needed to populate the dashboard

criteria.textContent: Run some workflows to start collecting LLM analytics

assertions.description: When there is no daily cost data, the Cost Over Time chart shows 'No daily cost data available' and 'Run some workflows to start tracking costs' instead of an empty chart
When there is no model cost data, the Cost by Model chart shows 'No model cost data available' instead of an empty chart
When there is no phase cost data, the Cost by Phase chart shows 'No phase cost data available' instead of an empty chart
When there is no latency data, the Provider Latency chart shows 'No latency data available' instead of an empty chart
When there is no task run cost data, the table shows 'No task run cost data available' and 'Costs will appear here after workflows run'

While cost trends data is being fetched from the web backend, the Cost Trends section shows its own spinning RefreshCw icon independently of the main dashboard loading state
